headline: Guinea asks France to return the skull of Bokar Biro, who led the resistance against French colonization
subhead: Conakry, Guinea's capital city, seeks to reclaim the skulls of the last ruler of the theocratic state of Fouta-Djallon and those of three of his close companions, nearly 130 years after their premeditated murder by French colonial troops.

headline: Tunisia, country of broken dreams: 'I wanted to photograph the young people whose lives began with the revolution'
subhead: 'Growing up in hostile environments' (3/7). Tunisian photographer Zied Ben Romdhane has documented his country since the fall of Ben Ali and the Arab Spring in late 2010. His work captures the deep malaise of a generation that has known only political turmoil and a lack of economic opportunities. Deprived of hope, on the edge of a sun-drenched sea, these young people dream solely of leaving.

headline: 'Why shouldn't I have the right to do what Angelina Jolie did?': Inside a breast surgery clinic in Paris
subhead: 'My Breasts and Me' (1/5). For aesthetic, social, medical or political reasons, some women want smaller breasts, or none at all – a growing number of requests that simply did not exist some 15 years ago. Le Monde spent several weeks at the Paris Breast Center Restitute to understand this changing trend.
